question: True or false: tilting polarised sunglasses can make parts of a rainbow almost vanish?
answer: True. Reflected inside each drop near the angle that polarises light most, rainbow light leaves about 96% polarised, vibrating along the arc. A polarising lens passes it one way and blocks it turned a quarter circle. Ordinary sunglasses, built to cut glare from the ground, erase the top of the arch and leave its ends.
move: A filter that seems neutral can quietly choose what you get to see.
ask: Which filter that seems neutral is choosing what I get to see?
trap: False, because sunglasses dim all light evenly.
reference: Können, Polarized Light in Nature, Cambridge University Press, 1985
